title: Find, Fix, Reason: Context Repair for Video Reasoning
one_liner: Use a stronger frozen teacher to add only the missing video evidence, then train the smaller student on the repaired context.
lead: A video question may fail not because the student model is generally weak, but because it missed one needed time span or region in the video. This paper builds a teacher that can inspect the original video, locate the missing evidence, and add a minimal patch to the student's context. The student answers again with that repaired evidence, and training rewards answers whose reasoning matches the supplied evidence because the goal is not only a correct answer but a correct answer grounded in the right part of the video.

problem.h2: Why many video reasoning errors are really missing-evidence errors
paras: A video question often depends on a short event, a distant dependency across time, or a small region in one frame. If the student model does not attend to that evidence, the final answer can be wrong even when the model has enough general reasoning ability to solve the question once the right evidence is present.

Current training approaches often push the student to explore or imitate whole solution traces. That can help final accuracy in some cases, but it does not directly repair the missing observation because the student still may not see the event or region that mattered. This paper instead changes the observation itself. It asks what minimal evidence patch would let the student see the relevant event or region and reason from it.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Use a frozen teacher with tools to locate the missing video evidence, add only that evidence to the student's context, and then train the student on the repaired attempt.

panels.title: 1. Student answers from incomplete context
panels.viz_args: The key event or region was not present in the student's working context
panels.caption: The failure may come from missing observation rather than from missing reasoning skill.

panels.title: 2. Teacher inspects the full video
panels.viz_args: Search the original video for the missing time span or region
panels.caption: The teacher has stronger observation ability because it can use tools to zoom in on the relevant evidence.

panels.title: 3. Teacher returns a small evidence patch
panels.caption: The patch is minimal because the goal is to add the missing dependency, not to rewrite the whole task.

panels.title: 4. Student answers again with repaired context
panels.caption: The new attempt is more likely to be correct because the student now sees the needed evidence.

panels.title: 5. Training rewards grounded improvement
panels.caption: Learning improves because success is tied both to the final answer and to whether the reasoning points back to the inserted evidence.

steps.text: Let the student answer the original question so that failure cases reveal which evidence may be missing.

steps.b: Ask the teacher to diagnose the gap
steps.text: Have the teacher search the full video for the missing time span or region that would repair the failed attempt.
Add only the missing evidence to the student's context because the question itself stays the same.
Collect a second answer and rationale so that training can compare the repaired attempt with the original one.
Update the student toward answers that are correct and supported by the cited repair evidence.

paras: The paper changes training from whole-trace imitation into observation-level repair guided by a stronger teacher because many failures come from missing evidence rather than from missing general reasoning ability.

hidden.name: Missing spatiotemporal dependency
paras: The hidden quantity is the exact missing dependency in the video: the time span, region, or cross-time relation that the student needed but did not bring into its working context. That missing dependency is not visible from the wrong answer alone.

The teacher estimates this hidden gap by reading the original video and comparing it with the student's failed attempt. That diagnosis matters because one small patch can repair the answer if it contains the evidence the student was missing.

heat.caption: Darker means the teacher sees that dependency as a stronger candidate for the missing evidence.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is the specific missing piece of video evidence.
The method repairs the student's context by inserting the missing spatiotemporal dependency rather than by replacing the whole reasoning process.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: change the observation before changing the answer
paras: A wrong answer can come from two different causes: the model may reason badly, or it may reason from incomplete evidence. Context repair targets the second cause directly. If the student already has enough reasoning skill, then adding the right patch can unlock the correct answer without rebuilding the whole model.

The reward design matters as well. If training cared only about the final answer, the student could improve by accidental shortcuts. Rewarding evidence-aligned rationales works better because it pushes the student to use the supplied patch, not merely to guess the answer after the teacher intervention.

stages.s: Train on corrected and grounded retry
Student answers improve because the missing evidence is restored

math.h2: Reward answers that improve for the right reason
math.words: Give higher reward when the repaired attempt is correct and when its explanation uses the evidence that the teacher added.
symbols: training reward for one repaired retry
benefit from getting the final answer right after the repair
credit when the rationale actually points to the inserted evidence
penalty for adding too much extra context instead of a minimal repair

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Original answer is wrong because the student missed the moment when the person puts the key on the table.
Patch A adds the exact late timestamp and crop. Answer gain 8, evidence alignment 4, patch cost 1, total 11.
Patch B adds a long unrelated segment. Answer gain 4, evidence alignment 1, patch cost 3, total 2.
The system prefers Patch A because it repairs the needed observation with little extra noise.

math.note: The paper uses a chosen-rollout training design with a reward for grounded improvement. This compact form states the same preference.

charts.title: Student without context repair
charts.note: Without repair, the student keeps missing key evidence, so both answers and justifications stay weaker.

charts.title: Find, Fix, Reason
charts.note: The reported trend makes sense because the teacher supplies the missing evidence and the reward encourages the student to use it.

items.html: If the teacher misdiagnoses the missing dependency, the patch may add irrelevant evidence, so the retry remains weak.
A large patch can hide the real cause of improvement because it may give away too much context instead of isolating the needed evidence.
The repair helps only if the student learns to use the added evidence, so alignment reward matters because accuracy alone may not force grounded reasoning.
The method is appealing because it turns many failures into observation repair problems, and those are often easier to fix than rebuilding the whole reasoning stack.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a toy video question set where each answer depends on one short event or one small region. Use a simple student that answers from a limited clip and a stronger teacher that can inspect the full video because the teacher needs access to the evidence the student missed. For each failed student answer, have the teacher choose a timestamp or crop as the repair patch, then run the student again with that patch attached.

The demo should show that repaired retries beat unrepaired retries because the missing evidence has been restored. It should also record whether the student cites the repaired evidence in its rationale so that the improvement can be traced to the patch rather than to a lucky guess.
demo.closing: The main proof is that a small evidence repair raises accuracy because it restores the missing observation that the student needed for the question.
